fields.title: An innovative method of treating rectal cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
The present level of medicine gives grounds for hope in a healthy future. Many conditions once considered incurable hold no fear today. That progress rests on the unceasing work of scientists, Israeli ones among them.

In recent years Israeli clinics have made increasing use of minimally invasive techniques with endoscopic and laparoscopic equipment. These developments have reached the standard programmes for treating tumours of the rectum. Where an open operation was once required, hard for the patient to bear and carrying a high risk of injury, the same work can now be done in a far gentler way.

Transanal endoscopic microsurgery (TEM) is an innovative method of treating rectal cancer. Israeli specialists observe that TEM is marked by rapid recovery, because it enters the body as little as possible. The procedure is carried out with a rectoscope through the anus, and no additional openings or incisions are made.

The method is widely used at the Assuta hospital for the resection of large polyps and malignant tumours. Compared with a conventional operation, TEM has substantial advantages:

  • There is no need to form a colostomy, or to cut the rectal sphincter during the procedure;
  • Less pain;
  • A low rate of complications after surgery;
  • A short stay in hospital.

Patients who undergo this procedure generally recover faster and are discharged sooner.

fields.title: Radiation therapy in the treatment of breast cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
The Assuta medical centre in Israel has introduced a change to its breast cancer treatment programme. The change concerns radiation therapy, which works by delivering the dose to a single point during the removal of the growth.

Patients no longer have to go through a long course lasting a month after surgery. The innovative technique makes it possible to deliver the dose precisely while the tumour is being removed, which considerably shortens recovery and spares the patient the side effects of radiation therapy.

According to Dr Dafna Barsuk, a senior specialist at the hospital, this treatment has considerable advantages: the tumour is irradiated precisely, and the beam does not extend beyond its edges. A great many post-operative processes are reduced to a minimum, which shortens the stay in hospital. The patient can return to her home country within a few weeks.

The innovative procedure can be carried out for any indication, whatever the size of the tumour and the age of the patient. The decision to use the method is taken on the basis of the diagnostic results and with the patient's consent.

fields.title: The TEM method: a new technology for treating rectal cancer in Israel
fields.bodyHtml:
TEM, or transanal endoscopic microsurgery, is a new and revolutionary method of treating rectal cancer in Israel. When operating to remove a malignant tumour, most Israeli clinics normally use the minimally invasive laparoscopic method. That technology allows the patient to recover quickly after the intervention, because the entry into the body causes little injury.

Recently, however, doctors at the Assuta clinic have begun removing tumours of the rectum by the TEM method. This method treats the cancer through the anus, without additional incisions, so recovery is faster still. TEM is used to treat cancer at an early stage and also to remove large polyps. The operation is performed with a rectoscope.

Advantages of the TEM method:

  • Less pain
  • A short period of required hospitalisation
  • A low rate of complications
  • No need to cut the rectal sphincter during the operation
  • A low proportion of operations that end in the formation of a colostomy

Many doctors at the Assuta clinic already perform operations by the TEM method, working to give patients treatment of the highest quality and effectiveness. Every patient of the clinic receives qualified care, round-the-clock attention and comfortable rooms while being treated in Israel.

fields.title: Darling, I want a boy — take an aspirin
fields.bodyHtml:
Taking aspirin raises the likelihood of having a boy. That is the conclusion of a study reported by The Daily Mail.

The study involved 1,228 women who had previously had miscarriages.

All the participants intended to become pregnant again. The researchers asked the women to take either low doses of aspirin or a placebo (folic acid) before sex.

As the newspaper reports, the authors of the study suggested that the miscarriages were linked to a high level of inflammation in the womb. One of the versions considered was that the immune system perceives the developing embryo as a foreign body and reacts aggressively to it.

The researchers proposed that inflammation reduces the chances of having a boy, given that male embryos are considered more vulnerable.

The study data allowed them to state that women who took aspirin before sex gave birth to boys more often than the participants who received the placebo (31 per cent against 23 per cent).

The checks also established that the level of inflammation fell in the women who took aspirin.

Original source: 9tv.co.il
